hook: Stir table salt into water and it seems to vanish. It is still there, split into ions, each wrapped in a shell of water molecules all turned the same way. Drawing that shell the wrong way round is one of the most common errors on the exam.

prereq.q: Which end of a water molecule carries a partial negative charge?
prereq.why: Oxygen is more electronegative and pulls the shared electrons toward itself.

options: An ion attracting the oppositely charged end of a polar molecule
A covalent bond between an ion and water
prereq.why: An ion attracts the opposite partial charge of a polar molecule.

prereq.q: What is the molarity of Cl⁻ in 0.10 M CaCl₂?
prereq.why: Each CaCl₂ gives two Cl⁻ ions.

figure.caption: Hydrated ions: water's oxygen faces a cation; a hydrogen faces an anion.

chain.cause: Water molecules are polar, with δ− O and δ+ H
chain.effect: they attract the ions at the surface of an ionic crystal

chain.cause: Ion-dipole attractions pull ions out of the lattice
chain.effect: the solid dissociates into separate ions
water points O toward cations and H toward anions, forming a hydration shell

chain.cause: Each formula unit gives a fixed set of ions
chain.effect: a correct diagram keeps the formula ratio and a total charge of zero

ideas: Dissolved ionic compounds are separate, hydrated ions; molecular solutes stay as whole molecules.
Water orientation: O (δ−) toward cations, H (δ+) toward anions.
Keep the formula ratio (CaCl₂: 1 Ca²⁺ to 2 Cl⁻) and keep polyatomic ions whole.
Spread solute particles evenly: a solution is homogeneous.

misconception.wrong: Water always points its oxygen toward a dissolved ion, because oxygen is the part of water that attracts things.
misconception.right: Water turns its δ− oxygen toward a cation but its δ+ hydrogens toward an anion. Like charges facing each other would repel.

summary: When an ionic compound dissolves, ion-dipole attractions pull it apart into separate ions, and each is hydrated: water's oxygen faces cations and its hydrogens face anions. A correct particle diagram shows separate ions in the formula ratio, whole polyatomic ions, an even spread and zero total charge; molecular solutes stay as whole molecules.
